items.value: Injecting a carbon dioxide + water mix into basalt to lock the gas up as limestone is a usable method of carbon sequestration
items.reasoning: The passage's whole point is that the injected carbon dioxide ends up chemically fixed in rock — 'carbon dioxide is converted into stone'. Permanently immobilising carbon dioxide underground is precisely carbon sequestration, so B is the practical suggestion the experiment implies. A misreads the aim: nobody would mine basalt and pump gas into it to manufacture cheap building limestone. C inverts the chemistry — the calcium and magnesium are dissolved OUT of the basalt as a side effect, not harvested as the goal. D fixates on an incidental step (the acidic mixture) and states no useful application at all.

items.value: Both assumptions are valid: icebergs affect Southern Ocean primary productivity and food chains, and their melting has climate and fishery consequences
items.reasoning: Assumption 1 is close to explicit: ocean colour is stated to indicate phytoplankton productivity, and phytoplankton growth IS primary production and the base of the marine food chain, so giant icebergs demonstrably bear on both. Assumption 2 follows from the two facts the passage supplies together — icebergs store up to 20 per cent of Southern Ocean carbon (a climate lever) and their melt water fertilises phytoplankton (the base of the fishery food chain) — so a change in iceberg melting must propagate to both. Runner-up is A (1 only), which wins if 'impact world fisheries' is judged too large a jump from a passage that never leaves the Southern Ocean and never mentions fish; the deciding word is 'world'.

items.value: The finding can be applied to develop clinically useful antimicrobial compounds
items.reasoning: The passage's own forward-looking sentence is the key: the find 'could throw new light on compounds associated with plant response to pathogens like fungi or bacteria'. Compounds a plant deploys against fungi and bacteria are antimicrobials, so B is the application the passage itself points at. A is absurd — corn caterpillars eat the crop, not weeds. D invents genetic modification the passage never raises. Runner-up is C (organic pesticides): it wins if the intended message is drawn from the first half of the passage (a natural insect-defence pathway could be exploited for eco-friendly crop protection) rather than from the closing sentence — but note the finding is that frass switches the plant's defence OFF, which is the wrong direction for building a pesticide, and 'pesticide' appears nowhere in the text.

32 = 2^5, so 32^5 = 2^25. Then 32^5 + 2^27 = 2^25(1 + 2^2) = 2^25 x 5 = 167772160. That has exactly the prime factors 2 and 5, so it is divisible by 10 but by none of 3, 7 or 11. Direct check: 167772160 / 10 = 16777216 exactly, while the number leaves remainders under 3, 7 and 11.

items.value: 5 — it is the smallest sum with two ordered pairs, (1,4) and (2,3)
items.reasoning: Enumerate the pairs of positive integers with p < q for each k. k = 3 gives only (1,2); k = 4 gives only (1,3), since (2,2) is barred by p < q. k = 5 gives both (1,4) and (2,3), so k = 5 is the first sum that fails to fix p and q. Hence 5. Option D (6) also fails to determine them, but it is not the smallest such value.

items.value: He walks South initially
items.reasoning: Trace the route from the house at the origin with the initial heading South: 100 m South reaches (0, -100); a left turn from South faces East, so 100 m gives (100, -100); a second left turn faces North, so 300 m gives (100, 200); a right turn from North faces East, so the final 100 m gives (200, 200). The office is equally far East and North of the house, i.e. exactly North-East. The other three headings were tested the same way and land at (-200, -200), (-200, 200) and (200, -200) — South-West, North-West and South-East respectively — so only South works.

items.value: He is now walking towards the North-East
items.reasoning: Take compass bearings with North = 0 degrees increasing clockwise. Walking West is a bearing of 270 degrees; a left turn is 90 degrees anticlockwise, giving 180 degrees, i.e. South. Turning 225 degrees clockwise from there gives 180 + 225 = 405, which reduces to 45 degrees — North-East. The 100 m distances are irrelevant to the direction asked for.

items.value: Neither conclusion follows: being the largest producer implies nothing about exports or imports
items.reasoning: Production volume says nothing about trade. A country can be the world's largest producer and still export very little because its own population consumes the output, so Conclusion I does not follow. Equally, a large domestic output does not preclude importing particular milk products or covering regional shortfalls, so Conclusion II does not follow either. Both conclusions add trade information that is simply absent from the statement.

items.value: Both statements together are needed; they fix m = 24 and n = 1
items.reasoning: Statement I alone leaves infinitely many pairs: whenever n = 1, m + 1 > m holds for every m, so (2,1), (3,1), (4,1) and so on all satisfy m + n > mn with m > n. Statement II alone leaves the eight factor pairs of 24. Combining them, only (24,1) survives, because 24 + 1 = 25 > 24 while 12 + 2 = 14, 8 + 3 = 11 and 6 + 4 = 10 all fall short of 24. So neither statement alone answers the question but the two together do.

items.value: Both statements together are needed; 12 MB at 2.4 KB/s takes 5120 seconds
items.reasoning: Time equals size divided by rate, so a size with no rate and a rate with no size are each useless on their own — neither statement alone can produce a time. Together, 12 megabytes is 12 x 1024 = 12288 kilobytes, and 12288 / 2.4 = 5120 seconds (about 85 minutes). Both statements are needed and both together suffice.

items.value: A responsible media must circulate reality without distortion in a democracy
items.reasoning: The passage closes on exactly this: 'A normatively responsible media through its communication effect has the responsibility to circulate the content of reality without distortion.' That is the crux, and A restates it. B contradicts the passage, which is about the real finding expression rather than fake news being inherent. C argues for unrestricted expression, a claim the passage never makes — it speaks of responsibility, not licence. D is a pessimistic assertion about control that appears nowhere in the text.

items.value: Interconnected home devices expose their owners to security and privacy risks
items.reasoning: The passage's concern is that manufacturers and service providers gather personal data 'with or without our agreement', turning the home into a corporate storefront, and that marketers have strong incentives to watch consumer behaviour. That is a privacy and data-security warning, which only D states. C states the opposite sentiment (comfort and quality of life) and A and B convert a warning about surveillance into a cheerful economic benefit, which reverses the passage's tone entirely.

items.value: High environmental standards are now a precondition for steady, sufficient and inclusive growth
items.reasoning: Green growth is presented as rethinking growth so that it survives a resource-constrained world: without resource-frugal strategies we face 'an economic dead end' (growth that is neither steady nor sufficient) or affluence for 'only a small elite ... in the midst of a sea of poverty' (growth that is not inclusive). C states precisely that environmental care is the prerequisite for such growth. A and B assume a trade-off between environment and growth that the passage is written to deny, and D is a counsel of despair the passage nowhere endorses.

items.value: Both statements together are needed; they fix x = 6 and y = 2
items.reasoning: Statement I alone admits endless pairs — (3,1), (5,1), (9,3), (10,2) and so on all give an odd quotient. Statement II alone leaves the six ordered pairs of distinct naturals with product 12. Testing those six against Statement I: 1/12, 2/6, 3/4 and 4/3 are not integers at all (and so not odd), 12/1 = 12 is even, and only 6/2 = 3 is odd. So the pair is uniquely (6,2), reachable only by using both statements.

items.value: Both statements together are needed; the shares are X = 4/9, Z = 1/3, Y = 2/9, so Y received the least
items.reasoning: Statement I gives X = (4/5)(Y + Z), so X is 4/9 of the total and Y + Z is 5/9 — but that split can be shared out in any way, so the least recipient could be Y or Z and cannot be named. Statement II likewise fixes Y at 2/9 while leaving X + Z = 7/9 unallocated, so the least could be Z. Using both, X = 4/9, Y = 2/9 and therefore Z = 1 - 4/9 - 2/9 = 3/9, and Y at 2/9 is unambiguously the smallest.

items.value: Even both statements together cannot give the number of students
items.reasoning: Neither statement carries any count. Statement I only bounds the marks between 50 and 70. Statement II only tells us that the two excluded marks average 60 between them, i.e. that the highest and lowest sum to 120 — which Statement I then merely confirms, since 70 + 50 = 120. Nothing in either statement, separately or together, constrains how many students lie between those extremes: a class of 3, of 30 or of 300 can each have mean 60 with a highest of 70 and a lowest of 50.

items.value: Statement I alone is enough (the numbers are 3, 5 and 11); Statement II alone is not
items.reasoning: The three primes cannot include 2, since 2 plus two odd primes is an even number greater than 2 and so composite. All three are therefore odd, and enumerating triples of distinct odd primes with sum below 23 gives 3+5+7 = 15 (composite), 3+5+11 = 19 (prime), 3+5+13 = 21 and 3+7+11 = 21 (both composite), with 5+7+11 = 23 and 3+7+13 = 23 already at the limit. Only {3, 5, 11} qualifies, so Statement I alone pins the numbers down. Statement II alone does not: {3,5,11}, {5,7,11}, {5,7,17} and many more contain 5 and have a prime sum.

items.value: Even both statements together cannot settle whether x + y is an integer
items.reasoning: Adding the two statements gives 3(x + y) as an integer, which only forces x + y to be a multiple of one-third, not a whole number. Concretely, x = y = 1/3 makes 2x + y = 1 and x + 2y = 1, both integers, while x + y = 2/3 is not; but x = 0, y = 1 also satisfies both statements and gives x + y = 1, which is. Since both answers are reachable with the statements fully in force, they cannot decide the question even jointly — and each alone is weaker still.

items.value: Both statements together are needed; they force p = r = 17
items.reasoning: Since q = 16 is the least of the three and the three cost 50 in all, p + r = 34 with neither p nor r below 16. Statement I says p is at most r, which with p + r = 34 gives p at most 17 — so p could be 16 or 17 and is not fixed. Statement II says r is at most p, which gives p at least 17 — so p could be 17 or 18 and is again not fixed. Taken together the two say p is at most r and r is at most p, hence p = r, and 2p = 34 gives p = 17. Note this is why the item prints two mirror-image inequalities: read strictly they combine into an equality that neither delivers alone.

items.value: Even both statements together cannot tell whether P scored more than Q
items.reasoning: Together the statements only yield S > Q and P > R (add and subtract the two relations), neither of which compares P with Q. A search over small values confirms both outcomes remain possible: P=10, Q=5, R=4, S=11 satisfies P+Q = R+S = 15 and P+S = 21 > Q+R = 9 with P above Q; while P=5, Q=10, R=4, S=11 satisfies the same two conditions (15 = 15 and 16 > 14) with P below Q. Since both cases survive, the question is unanswerable even with both statements.

items.value: Poetry is a form of dynamic resistance against tyranny and the arrogance of power
items.reasoning: The passage builds to two closing sentences that are its message: 'Against the tyranny of truth, poetry remains a partisan of democratic reality. Against the arrogance of power, wealth and hierarchy, poetry proposes both humility and defiance.' Defiance against tyranny and arrogance is exactly resistance, which is D. B and C are eliminated outright — the passage never calls poetry anathema to truth, nor does it reduce poetry to romance and feeling. Runner-up is A (poetry accepts imperfections), which draws on the genuine middle of the passage ('Truth usually does not admit any contradictions or imperfections ... Poetry abides by the plurality of life'); A would win if the crux is taken to be the truth-versus-plurality contrast rather than the closing call to defiance, though A also narrows 'life and existence' to 'humans', which the text does not.

items.value: Neither assumption is valid — the author treats flowers as functional adaptations, and their beauty as the incidental by-product
items.reasoning: The passage argues the opposite of Assumption 1: petals and perfume exist to attract an insect so that pollen is transferred efficiently and 'not wasted', which is thrift and utility rather than Nature's luxury. Assumption 2 is inverted too: the author explicitly locates the flower's usefulness in pollination and dismisses beauty as 'merely a by-product and a human invention', so it is beauty, not usefulness, that he declines to treat as real. Both assumptions therefore reverse the author's position.

items.value: Statement II alone is enough (the ages are 51 and 15, difference 36); Statement I alone is not
items.reasoning: Write the ages as 10a + b and 10b + a. Their sum is 11(a + b) and their difference is 9|a - b|. Statement II makes 11(a + b) = (11/6) x 9|a - b|, which simplifies to 2(a + b) = 3|a - b|; the only digit pair satisfying this is {5, 1}, giving ages 51 and 15 and a difference of 36 — a full search over all two-digit reversible pairs returns exactly this one difference. Statement I alone only says which of the two is older, leaving the difference as any of 9, 18, 27, ... 72. So one statement alone answers it and the other does not.

items.value: Both ordered pairs SP and RQ are valid implications consistent with the main statement
items.reasoning: The main statement asserts the disjunction 'Director or Producer'. From S ('not a Producer') the disjunction forces P ('is a Director'), so SP is a valid implication; from R ('not a Director') it forces Q ('is a Producer'), so RQ is valid too. Both are also consistent with the main statement, since each merely selects one of its two permitted cases. The conclusion holds whether the 'either ... or' is read inclusively or exclusively, so both pairs qualify.

Substituting the coded operators simultaneously turns + into -, - into x, x into division and division into +, so 10 + 30 - 100 x 50 divided by 25 becomes 10 - 30 x 100 divided by 50 + 25. Applying the usual order of operations, 30 x 100 = 3000 and 3000 divided by 50 = 60, leaving 10 - 60 + 25 = -25. (Multiplication and division rank equally, so evaluating them left to right or the division first both give 60, and the result is unchanged.)
